messages:
alex: Seeing a spike of GPU pod evictions in us-west1 tonight. Starts ~2198765400. Not all pods show the same reason, but pattern emerges.
mina: any common node attrs? instance type / taints?
alex: quick grep: evictions mostly on nodes with nic.driver=ixgbevf and kernel 6.1.x. Some show CNI errors right before pod was evicted. Example event dump:
```
Warning  NetworkUnavailable  pod/train-abc  NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod "train-abc": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to add conlink: nic-driver crash
Warning  FailedScheduling    pod/train-abc  0/22 nodes are available: 7 Insufficient memory, 5 Insufficient gpu, 10 network plugin not ready.
Normal   Preempted         pod/train-abc  Preempted by pod/interactive-shell (priority class high-debug)
```

tj: so three things: NIC driver flaps -> Node becomes NotReady / CNI broken -> scheduler marks as unschedulable -> when debug pod lands it preempts.
ravi: also noticed our topologySpreadConstraint is forcing spread across AZs for batch namespace, creating single-GPU leftovers on many nodes. This increases chance a 4-GPU debug lands and preempts.
mina: what's the distribution of contiguous free GPUs? can we get a histogram?
alex: ran a quick scrape: 50 nodes total in pool, free gpus per node: [0,0,1,1,2,4,0,1,0,2, ...] -> 42% of free GPUs are singletons. high fragmentation.
ops-oncall: I can do a manual compact/evict run in the 00:30 UTC window tonight if we want.
tj: proposed hotfixes (short):
- reduce PriorityClass of interactive-shell in prod to avoid large-scale preemptions (rollback high-debug -> medium)
- deploy a short descheduler job with RemoveDuplicates and LowNodeUtilization to consolidate 1-GPU batch pods onto spot pool for 20m
- cordon nodes with repeated nic.driver crash traces and escalate to infra for kernel/driver pin
- add a temporary podAffinity rule for batch namespace to prefer packing (affinity weight high)
ravi: agree on (1) and (3) now. (2) is fine but watch autoscaler thrash. affinity change needs canary.
mina: cost note: forcing packing onto A100s will likely bump on-demand usage and cost. But it reduces preemption/timeouts for long-running jobs. Tradeoff ok for short window.
alex: infra notes: driver crash correlates with a recent kernel update image rolled to us-west1 nodes 2026-03-15. Ops: can we pin older kernel for that pool until vendor patch?
ops-oncall: I can pin and repro in canary. For hotfix tonight I'll cordon 6 most-flapping nodes, drain low-priority pods, and run descheduler.
tj: longer term: we should add a scheduler scoring plugin that rewards contiguous GPU slots (soft binpack). Also consider gang scheduling or node-level GPU reservation to avoid 1-GPU scattering.
ravi: also add a NetworkWatchdog that marks nodes NotReady if CNI restarts >3 times in 5m, to avoid partial schedules onto flappy nodes.
mina: can someone run the fragmentation query and paste stats to ticket? I want exact numbers for before/after compact.
alex: done, uploaded CSV to INF-4899 and linked grafana panel showing preemptions by priority.
ops-oncall: running compact tonight 00:30 UTC. Steps: 1) cordon suspected nodes; 2) drain low-priority pods w/30s grace; 3) run descheduler job for 20m; 4) uncordon. Will watch preemptions and autoscaler.
tj: +1. I'll open RFC for PackScore scheduler plugin (owner: tj, target Q3).
infra-bot: infra-bot detected a kernel-image rollout to us-west1-gpu-pool on 2026-03-15T04:12:00Z (change id: roll-20260315-ker), flagging nodes with ixgbevf and kernel 6.1.x.
alex: thanks. Follow-ups: (a) mina lower debug priority in prod now, (b) ops-oncall run compact, (c) infra pin kernels for flappy pool and validate vendor fix. I'll update INF-4899 after compact. :thumbsup:
